summary: Scene state is what a scene remembers beyond its text, kept so that regenerating, choosing a version, cutting, restoring and forking all leave it where the shown history says. A piece of state is a slot declared in one file and listed by a generator. What one reply version changed in a slot is a delta, a value at a path rather than an operation, stored on that version by swipe id so a fork shares its prefix's deltas without copying them. The state is rebuilt from the shown versions, from the nearest keyframe, inside the transaction of whatever changed the history. Slots are single files (the macro variables and the chat summary), one list made from the module table (the Props trackers, whose Story Director updates, Spellbook tick and the person's edits all go through the same two write doors), and two families that serve the library trackers a scene links, whose state a tracker's update tool writes as pending deltas on the reply being written. Its sections cover slots, deltas and the three strategies, storage, rebuild, how a turn uses it (with the variables route and the chat import), the Props trackers, the chat summary, global variables derived from every scene's shown versions, who may write each slot, what is not built yet, and what is tested. A range read of the same data shows what each message changed.

sections.title: Slots
sections.summary: A slot is one file under src/core/scene-state/slots that exports defineSlot with an id, a scope, a diff strategy and a default. defineSlot refuses an id outside the allowed pattern and a keyed-list without a key. The command bun run slots writes the generated list from the folder, slots:check fails when it is stale, and a completeness test fails when a slot file is missing from the list or an id repeats. The only scope is scene, meaning rebuilt from history. The vars slot uses the fields strategy, so each variable keeps the time it was first written and the time it was last written, which is exactly what the macro engine's variable record holds. A slot may declare a shape, the rule every value written to it passes, so the stores refuse a malformed value and an undeclared slot. The summary slot is described in its own section, and the Props trackers' slots are the first child below. The family form, for state made by library pieces, is the child section below.

children.title: The Props trackers' slots
children.summary: Each Props tracker module that keeps state, the twelve legacy trackers, has one slot named tracker.module, made from the module table by one slot file that exports a list; the four Storyboards keep only a setting. A module with a list of rows keeps one wrapper row per list row and per other field in a keyed-list slot; a module with no list keeps one field per delta. A slot's shape comes from the module's own shapes. Whole-state rules stay with the module's parse, and each module has one repair step in its read that keeps every field it can and brings a broken rule inside, so a cut never makes a read show the defaults.

children.title: Slot families
children.summary: A slot id ending in a colon and a star is a family covering every id with that prefix, so state made by a library piece at run time needs no file of its own and the store never sees library pieces. The slot lookup gives the exact slot if there is one, else the family whose prefix the id has. A family id is one lowercase word, a colon and a star; its file is named without them, and overlapping or repeated families fail the generator. Two exist, tracker-record with the fields strategy and tracker-list with the keyed-list strategy keyed by name; a tracker's own value shape is checked in the core tracker module.

sections.title: Deltas and the three strategies
sections.summary: A delta names a slot, a path inside it, a value or a removal marker, and the time of the write. It is always a value, never an operation, so cutting a middle message takes back exactly what that message set and nothing a later message set again. Three strategies cut and fold deltas: value keeps the whole value, fields keeps one delta per named field, and keyed-list keeps one delta per row found by a key field. Fields holds the variables, keyed-list holds the summary and the linked list trackers, and all three are implemented and tested. Fold skips a delta for an unknown slot or with a path its strategy cannot read, and the stores refuse such a delta outright. A variable named like an Object property is an ordinary own property.

sections.title: Storage
sections.summary: Migration 43 adds five tables and an index. swipe_deltas holds one row per delta keyed by swipe id and sequence and is never changed once written, so a fork that keeps swipe ids shares its prefix's deltas. message_deltas holds what a message carries, and migration 44 adds a swipe id to it: null is a person's edit, and a swipe id is a write made after a commit that names its version, kept with this take's message so a fork copies it. branch_base is what a take starts with, real data that refuses when damaged. branch_state is each take's tip cache, and state_keyframes keeps the whole state after every fiftieth shown message; both are caches rebuilt when unreadable. Paths, values, keyframes and pending deltas are sealed like other chat payloads. The tables join the row fingerprints, the health check and the snapshot lists. A version has no size cap on its deltas; only what an import or a person's edit brings meets a hostile-input ceiling.

sections.title: Rebuild
sections.summary: The store owns the rebuild and runs it inside the transaction of the change, so no caller can forget it. It starts from the nearest kept keyframe on the shown path, else the take's base, else nothing, folds the deltas of the shown versions after it in order, rewrites the keyframes it passes and writes the tip cache. Committing a reply, adding or choosing a version, and cutting or restoring each rebuild from the message they changed; a fork rebuilds the new take, and deleting a take drops its cache. recordDeltas keeps a write that names a version with this take's message and rebuilds that take only. A continue stamps no delta, and a failed turn has stamped nothing. sceneStateBefore answers what a new version of a message builds from. sceneDeltas is a range read of the same data: the state before the first message without its own deltas, and each live message's deltas in fold order, changing nothing.

sections.title: How a turn uses it
sections.summary: loadTurn reads the variables from sceneState for a new reply and from sceneStateBefore for a new version or a continue, so a regenerate never counts its own earlier writes twice. Assembly returns the local variable changes, and scene-turn turns them into vars deltas saved on the checkpoint with the trace; commitTurn stamps them on the version it stores and rebuilds the take. A continue makes no deltas. The library's global variables ride the same pending set, so nothing is written before the request. The trackers' update tool and the skills' open_skill and close_skill add deltas mid-reply through the turn's one door, for the tracker slots and the skills slot only, as the loop's stateScoped writes; a skill's close rule closes it with the turn's own deltas. A write of a value the message already shows, its version's deltas included, adds nothing, so a person's tracker edit back to the value before a reply is kept on the tip message.

sections.title: The Props trackers
sections.summary: Every writer of a module's state goes through the two doors. The turn's own writes wait on the checkpoint and are stamped when the reply commits; the Spellbook's tick is computed in the turn, never on Stop or Continue, so a new version ticks once and a cut takes the tick with the reply. The Story Director's background round writes for the reply's version with recordDeltas, guarded by what it planned against; a field the person edited on that reply stays theirs, and the module's read repair never overrides that edit, so the module's update is skipped with a line in the activity. The person writes on the newest reply with recordMessageDeltas, several modules all or nothing, guarded by the stored values so a field the repair adjusted can still be edited. Anything the person clicks or accepts is that write, a cast rides only the next reply, and Undo writes the earlier data as the person's own edit.

sections.title: The chat summary
sections.summary: The summary slot is a keyed-list with a declared row shape and two layers that never write the same path. Generated pieces are rows keyed by the swipe id of the version they end at, written after the reply lands on that version in this take: an Every-exchange line is the row of its reply, and a rolling recap, growing timeline or backfill is a replacing block that removes the other generated rows, so regenerating or cutting its message gives them back. The person's text is one separate row written as an edit of the newest message, with a fresh edit id and the next number on every save. Each generated row records the id and number it saw, which orders the layers without a clock: rows that saw an older text are covered however many there are, and rows written after, or that saw a newer save since deleted, show. A fork inherits the prefix and its writes stay in the fork.

sections.title: Global variables
sections.summary: The library's global variables are derived from every scene at once. A reply's global writes are operations (set, inc, append or delete) on the version that made them in the shared global slot, stamped at commit, so a failed or dropped turn writes none and a continue writes none of its own. A take's own fold skips a shared slot. A global's value is the fold, in write order, of the operations of every version shown in at least one live take, each counted once however many takes show it, leaving out cut versions and deleted takes or scenes. A new version of a reply builds without the version it replaces. Each operation is the write as the macro or lore Side Effect made it, so a set stays a set and two scenes that add to one number both count; a stored row that is not an operation refuses the read. The old variables document is no longer used, and the read is measured at about 110 ms for 10,000 operations, with no cache.

sections.title: Who may write
sections.summary: Every slot names who may write it, and every store door is one writer decided by the door, never by a request: a turn's checkpoint is the reply, recordDeltas a background writer such as the Story Director or the summary's writer, recordMessageDeltas the person, and setBranchBase an import. A delta whose slot does not name that writer refuses the whole write with a sentence. A guard test holds who may call each door and the only places that insert delta rows. Two separations sit above the store: the background class covers both the Story Director and the summary's writer, kept apart by the guard on who calls recordDeltas, and a model's tool is held to library tracker slots by the turn's write door. The Compendium writes lorebooks after checking each book's access level, so it needs no slot. A wrong write is undone by a swipe or a cut.

sections.title: Not built yet
sections.summary: Planned in the scene-state plan and absent from the code: lorebooks copied on fork (built and taken back out, waiting on decisions about per-scene settings, the Compendium wing and copies in the Library), a person's own edit of a global variable, the extension contract and a per-slot tier, which wait for an extension runtime and its manifest, the Story Director updating library trackers, hand edits of any slot other than a library tracker's, a Props tracker's and the summary, and a state inspector. The person's write door is recordMessageDeltas, called by the library tracker edit, the Props tracker write (an accepted Refresh included) and the person's summary text. The door for a write that names a version after its commit is recordDeltas, called by the chat summary's writer and the Story Director's tracker round. A slot's declared shape is checked on every delta either door takes, and a guard test holds the list of callers.

sections.title: What is tested
sections.summary: Unit proofs cover each strategy, the fold and a keyframe rebuild. The contract suite runs on both stores: versions, cuts, restores, forks, turns, refusals and a 2,000-message rebuild held to a 200 ms budget. The SQLite file adds shared delta rows, keyframes, sealing and the dense case. A busy-library test runs a real turn with the write lock held. The Props trackers have their own contract suite on both stores, a core test of cutting into deltas and back, turn tests for the prompt and the Spellbook's tick, two Director round suites, and a suite for the person's write over a repaired state. The chat summary, the range read and the global variables have their own suites, the macro engine is held to recording each global write as the operation it was, and who may write is held on both stores and by a guard on who calls each door. A guard test holds recordDeltas to its callers: the two stores, their contract files including the tracker-state one, the summary's writer and the Director's tracker round.
